title: Streckfus boat bands, Astoria Hot 8 recording, and leaving for Chicago
summary: Ten-piece boat band, Fate Marable, Desvigne and Piron, first recording with Lee Collins, then stranded in St. Louis in 1938 and staying in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: At that time I was born for the Stikker Steamboat Company. Uh-huh. And there was a ten piece band. It had three sax, three brass, and four rhythms. And you had to play banjo, you had to play pangeline guitar. If you were bass, you had to play bass following and bass horn. I worked with, I started with Fate Marble, and then they had a job with Sidney Desveen, and that's where he came to me. We used to play at the country club on Sundays. And that's where the Captain Vaughan came in and heard the band and I used to put on them, so we got the job with them. Which band? No, Sidney Desveen got the job, I'm sorry, because he was already working. They had another book called, something from Cincinnati down there. And his band should play, he was having trouble with them, so he hired me. I was working on top of the Astoria. Lee Collins, that's when I recorded that thing they called it, Astoria Hot 8. We had Sid Averdino clan, that white man. That's what we call that the old Italian Hall. That's the first recording I ever made. So from there, I went with Sidney and went on the boat there. Sidney got the job on the boat. And then I worked with Sidney, I don't know, one or two years. And then I went with A.J. Peer on. And then, it was Friday, 38, they dropped us off in St. Louis, gave us a train ticket to go back to New Orleans. And I went to the captain I was visiting. I stayed around St. Louis for a while. And I told the captain I'd like to visit New Orleans. So I went to Chicago, I mean. So I went to Chicago, a buddy of mine, he's married, and he had family, and had a room, and so he asked me to stop with him. So I ended up staying up there, 30 years to 40 years.
Yeah, for about ten years. And that's when you.
I was doing all combo work. I wasn't playing no band in there.
